findings.where: First screen, the 'Write to me' margin note (the page's one call to action, a mailto link), at desktop left of the red margin line, at phone between the intro and the photo
findings.fault: The page's one action is styled as a small handwritten note with a red pen line, so it looks like a margin annotation rather than a button. On desktop it sits in the margin, the strip a reader skips, at a fraction of the weight of the headline, the clipped photo and the aqueduct drawing, so the page's task order does not match its visual order. The tile also has no button anywhere: the brief's build scope asks for one, and the only other control, 'Replay the note', is underlined text. That leaves the layout round with no button signifier to place a 'Get in touch' with.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who came to find a consultant and wants to get in touch looks for a button near the headline and finds nothing button-like. The founder and the layout round need a defined button for the one action the brand sheet names.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Write to me' note's write-in motion (motion sketch timeline: hold up to 2,500 ms, then 900 ms to write)
findings.fault: The only call to action is held blank until every font has loaded, for up to 2.5 s, and then takes almost another second to write in. For as long as 3.4 s the first screen has no visible way to contact Mark, and a visitor who scans and moves on in that time never sees it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a slow office or field connection, typical for development-agency staff abroad, who reads the first screen as having no contact route.

findings.where: First screen, 'Write to me' (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com), and the nav's 'Contact' (href #)
findings.fault: There are two routes to Mark, and both fail some visitors. The note opens only a desktop mail client and never shows the address, so a visitor on webmail or a locked-down work machine gets nothing or an unconfigured mail app and cannot copy the address. The nav's 'Contact' link is dead, unlike 'Write to me', which at least points somewhere, so the same intent leads to one working route and one dead one.
findings.who_objects: A bank or agency officer on Outlook Web or Gmail in a browser who clicks to write and has no address to copy.

findings.where: Article specimen, the PDF row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge — Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'
findings.fault: The link is bold text in the same ink as the headings, and its only underline runs into the row's full-width bottom rule, so it reads as a static row in a table of documents rather than a link to a download. The 'Lecture · date · PDF' cell beside it looks equally inert. A visitor can't tell the row is the way to the paper.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's article who wants the lecture and doesn't see that the row can be clicked. Angélique's added PDFs would inherit the same hidden link.

findings.fault: A button that acts in place is styled as an underlined text link. The underline is the link's reserved carrier, so it looks as if it navigates away.
findings.who_objects: A reviewer or the layout round taking the tile as the signifier set: it teaches that an underline can mean either 'go' or 'do'.
